title: Ban Targeted Advertising? An Empirical Investigation of the Consequences for App Development
data_provenance_note: README: data under NDA, released under MS policy 4a with disguised identifiers (app_num, genre_num); variable values appear to be the original data.
eligible_reason: Single adoption date. Google Play's ban of targeted advertising in children's apps applies to all treated apps at the same month: in at.dta (5,834 apps, ym 700-722), TREATXAFTER first equals 1 in ym 713 for 2,827 of 2,834 treated apps; the remaining 7 first appear in the unbalanced panel later and are not separate policy cohorts. TREATXAFTER = Treat x AFTER is a two-group single-date DiD, so the at-least-two-cohorts rule fails. Table 2 col 1 has only app FE (xtreg, fe), month FE and genre dummies; cols 2-3 add time-varying controls (Log_Demand Age Price Log_Firm_Size One_Employee) and a lagged outcome. Tables 3, 5 add subgroup-by-treatment interactions; Table 9 is an event study i.ym##ann_TREAT around the same single date.
design_notes: App-month panel of Google Play apps. Treat = developer affected by the ban (Designed for Families apps); AFTER = months from the ban onward (ym >= 713, i.e. June 2019 in Stata %tm). Outcomes: Feature_Update, Rating, Log_Demand, Log_Price, File_Size, Permissions; Table 6 discontinued apps (cross-section OLS), Table 7 new game releases, Table 8 different dataset (tt.dta), Table 10 alternative samples (zac*.dta).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Verified from at.dta: one policy month (ym 713); 7 late entrants are panel-entry artifacts.

specs.exclusion_reason: single adoption date (ym 713 for all treated apps)
specs.notes: Cols 2-3 add time-varying controls and lagged outcome.

screener_notes: Screened from package only (readme.docx, do.do, at.dta inspected for treatment timing). No article text available.
